meta.description: Detailed historical timeline of quantum science, from the 17th-century debate on the nature of light to modern quantum computing. Each event card: year, people, discovery, evidence, significance. Track field forks into 'computing' at 1980.

acts.title: The nature of light
acts.theme: Newton vs Huygens: is light a particle or a wave? The 250-year argument quantum will end by answering 'both'.

acts.title: Cracks in the classical world
acts.theme: Waves win, atoms emerge, spectra appear - and classical physics starts failing to explain its own data.

acts.title: The quantum is born
acts.theme: Planck's desperate act to Einstein's photon to Bohr's atom: energy comes in packets.

acts.title: Quantum mechanics proper
acts.theme: A complete theory in five explosive years - matrices, waves, uncertainty, antimatter - then war-forged QED.

acts.title: Entanglement gets real
acts.theme: Bell turns philosophy into experiment; lasers and reversible-computing ideas quietly load the next revolution.

acts.title: The quantum computing era
acts.theme: The track forks: information becomes physical, algorithms threaten cryptography, machines get built.

events.title: Law of refraction
events.discovery: Precise mathematical law for how light bends when passing between media (sin ratios constant).
events.evidence: Geometric measurements of refraction angles across air-water-glass interfaces.
events.significance: First hint that light obeys exact mathematical law - the tradition of quantifying light begins here.

events.title: Diffraction of light
events.discovery: Light bends slightly around obstacles and produces fringed shadows; he coined the word 'diffraction'.
events.evidence: Sunbeam through tiny apertures cast shadows wider than geometry allowed, with colored fringes (published posthumously, Physico-mathesis de lumine).
events.significance: First observed behavior of light that particles-in-straight-lines could not explain - the earliest experimental seed of wave-particle trouble.

events.title: Pulse theory and thin-film colors
events.discovery: Proposed light as fast vibrations/pulses in a medium; studied iridescent colors of thin films (Micrographia).
events.evidence: Observations of colors in soap films, mica flakes and peacock feathers that vary with thickness.
events.significance: Early wave-like thinking about light; thin-film interference will later become a classic wave proof.

events.title: Dispersion and the corpuscular theory
events.discovery: White light is a mixture of colors separated by a prism; light is composed of particles ('corpuscles'). Full theory in Opticks (1704).
events.evidence: The famous prism experiments at Cambridge: a second prism recombines the spectrum back into white light.
events.significance: Newton's authority makes the particle theory dominant for over a century - the position quantum mechanics will partially vindicate.

events.title: Light has a finite speed
events.discovery: Light travels at a finite (enormous) velocity rather than instantaneously.
events.evidence: Timing anomalies in the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io depending on Earth-Jupiter distance.
events.significance: Light becomes a physical thing with measurable properties, not an abstract ray.

events.title: Wave theory of light
events.discovery: Light is a wave propagating through a medium; every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets (Huygens principle, Traite de la Lumiere).
events.evidence: Wave construction correctly derives reflection, refraction, and the strange double refraction of Iceland spar.
events.significance: The great rival to Newton's corpuscles. The particle-vs-wave duel is now formally open - it will take until 1905-1927 to resolve as 'both'.

events.title: Infrared radiation
events.discovery: Invisible 'heat rays' exist beyond the red end of the spectrum.
events.evidence: A thermometer placed past the red edge of a prism's spectrum rose higher than in visible light.
events.significance: The spectrum extends beyond human sight - radiation is a broader phenomenon than visible light, setting up the blackbody problem.

events.title: Double-slit interference
events.discovery: Light passing through two slits produces alternating bright and dark fringes - unambiguous wave interference.
events.evidence: The double-slit experiment (demonstrations and Royal Society lectures, 1801-1803).
events.significance: The wave theory's decisive blow against Newton's corpuscles - and the very experiment that will later, with single electrons and photons, become the central mystery of quantum mechanics.

events.title: Dark lines in the solar spectrum
events.discovery: The Sun's spectrum is crossed by hundreds of fixed dark lines at precise wavelengths.
events.evidence: High-quality prisms and diffraction gratings resolving 570+ lines, which he catalogued.
events.significance: A barcode written in sunlight with no explanation. Spectral lines become the central unexplained data that Bohr's quantum atom will finally decode in 1913.

events.title: Mathematical wave optics and the Poisson spot
events.discovery: Complete wave theory of diffraction; predicted (via Poisson's objection) a bright spot at the center of a circular shadow.
events.evidence: Arago experimentally found the 'impossible' bright spot, converting the objection into a triumph.
events.significance: Wave theory becomes quantitatively predictive; a rival's ridicule turned into proof - a template for how quantum theory will also win.

events.title: Light responds to magnetism
events.discovery: A magnetic field rotates the polarization of light passing through glass (Faraday rotation).
events.evidence: Polarized light through heavy glass between electromagnet poles showed measurable rotation.
events.significance: First direct link between light and electromagnetism - the clue Maxwell will turn into a full theory.

events.title: Spectroscopy and the blackbody problem
events.discovery: Each chemical element emits/absorbs its own unique set of spectral lines; Kirchhoff also poses the ideal 'blackbody' radiation problem.
events.evidence: Flame spectra of elements matched to Fraunhofer's solar lines, identifying elements in the Sun.
events.significance: Two time bombs planted at once: unexplained atomic fingerprints, and the blackbody spectrum whose solution in 1900 will detonate the quantum revolution.

events.title: Light is an electromagnetic wave
events.discovery: Unified electricity and magnetism into field equations whose wave solutions travel at exactly the speed of light.
events.evidence: Calculated wave speed from purely electrical measurements matched the measured speed of light.
events.significance: The crowning triumph of classical physics - and the theory whose collision with thermodynamics (blackbody) and with atoms (stability) will force the quantum.

events.title: The periodic table
events.discovery: Elements arranged by weight show repeating chemical patterns; gaps predicted new elements.
events.evidence: Successful predictions of gallium, scandium and germanium with correct properties.
events.significance: A pattern with no mechanism. Only quantum mechanics (Pauli exclusion + electron shells, 1925) will explain WHY the table repeats.

events.title: The hydrogen line formula
events.discovery: The visible spectral lines of hydrogen fit a simple integer formula - wavelengths depend on whole numbers.
events.evidence: Four measured hydrogen lines matched his formula to extraordinary precision; it then predicted further lines correctly.
events.significance: Integers hiding inside an atom's light. Nobody knows why for 28 years - until Bohr derives the formula from quantized orbits.

events.title: Radio waves confirmed - and a strange side effect
events.discovery: Generated and detected Maxwell's electromagnetic waves; also noticed that ultraviolet light makes sparks jump more easily (the photoelectric effect).
events.evidence: Spark-gap transmitter and resonant receiver loops; UV illumination of electrodes changed spark behavior.
events.significance: The same year confirms light-as-EM-wave AND stumbles on the effect that will prove light is particles. History's neatest irony.

events.title: No luminiferous ether
events.discovery: The expected 'ether wind' from Earth's motion does not exist - light's speed is the same in all directions.
events.evidence: Interferometer sensitive to fractions of a fringe found no seasonal or directional shift.
events.significance: If light is a wave, what waves? The medium is gone. Cracks open for both relativity and the photon.

events.title: X-rays
events.discovery: A penetrating, invisible radiation produced by cathode-ray tubes.
events.evidence: Fluorescent screen glowing across the room; the famous photograph of his wife's hand bones.
events.significance: New radiation beyond all known light - later shown to be high-energy photons, and the probe Compton will use to prove photon momentum.

events.title: Radioactivity
events.discovery: Uranium (then polonium and radium, isolated by the Curies) spontaneously emits energetic radiation.
events.evidence: Photographic plates fogged by uranium salts in total darkness; painstaking chemical isolation of new elements.
events.significance: Atoms are not eternal or indivisible - they transform and release energy from within. The atom's interior becomes physics' next frontier.

events.title: Wien's radiation laws
events.discovery: Displacement law (hotter bodies peak at shorter wavelengths) and a radiation formula that fits the short-wavelength side of the blackbody spectrum.
events.evidence: Careful blackbody cavity measurements at Berlin's PTR laboratory.
events.significance: Half a correct answer. The failure of any classical formula to fit the WHOLE spectrum is the precise crack Planck will fill with the quantum.

events.title: Discovery of the electron
events.discovery: Cathode rays are streams of a universal negative particle ~1800x lighter than hydrogen.
events.evidence: Deflection of cathode rays by electric and magnetic fields yielding charge-to-mass ratio.
events.significance: The first subatomic particle - the entity whose quantum behavior (orbits, spin, waves, exclusion) the entire theory will be built to describe.

events.title: The ultraviolet catastrophe
events.discovery: Classical physics, applied honestly to blackbody radiation, predicts infinite energy at short wavelengths - an absurdity.
events.evidence: Rayleigh-Jeans law fits long wavelengths but diverges catastrophically in the ultraviolet.
events.significance: Classical physics formally breaks. The stage is set: someone must do something desperate. Planck does, the same year.

events.title: The quantum of action (December 14, 1900)
events.discovery: Blackbody radiation is explained only if energy is exchanged in discrete packets E = h*nu, introducing the constant h.
events.evidence: His formula fit the entire measured blackbody spectrum perfectly, at all wavelengths and temperatures.
events.significance: The birthday of quantum theory. Planck called it 'an act of desperation' - he never expected the quantum to be real. It was.

events.title: Light quanta - the photon
events.discovery: Light itself consists of discrete energy quanta; this explains the photoelectric effect's dependence on frequency, not intensity.
events.evidence: Photoelectric data: electron energy rises with light frequency and has a sharp threshold - impossible for classical waves.
events.significance: Newton's corpuscles return, transformed. Einstein's only self-described 'revolutionary' paper - and his Nobel Prize (1921), not relativity.

events.title: Quantum theory of solids
events.discovery: Quantized vibrations explain why the heat capacity of solids drops at low temperature, violating classical predictions.
events.evidence: Einstein's model matched anomalous specific-heat data (later refined by Debye, 1912).
events.significance: Proof the quantum isn't just about light - MATTER is quantized too. The quantum becomes universal.

events.title: Charge comes in units
events.discovery: Electric charge is quantized: every measured charge is an integer multiple of e.
events.evidence: The oil-drop experiment (1909-1913): balancing charged droplets against gravity in an electric field.
events.significance: Discreteness confirmed at the level of charge itself. (Millikan later verifies Einstein's photoelectric equation while trying to disprove it.)

events.title: The atomic nucleus
events.discovery: Atoms are mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus.
events.evidence: Gold-foil experiment: ~1 in 8000 alpha particles bounced backward - 'as if you fired a shell at tissue paper and it came back'.
events.significance: Creates an impossible atom: classical electrons orbiting a nucleus must radiate and crash within nanoseconds. Something non-classical keeps atoms alive.

events.title: First Solvay Conference
events.discovery: The world's leading physicists convene specifically on 'Radiation and the Quanta' - the first conference of the quantum age.
events.evidence: Brussels, October 1911; the iconic photograph of classical physics' elite confronting the quantum.
events.significance: The quantum problem is now THE problem of physics, no longer a curiosity.

events.title: The quantized atom
events.discovery: Electrons occupy only discrete orbits with quantized angular momentum; light is emitted in jumps between them.
events.evidence: Derived Balmer's 1885 hydrogen formula from first principles, with the Rydberg constant emerging from h, e, and m.
events.significance: The 28-year-old mystery of hydrogen's integer spectrum solved. Atoms are stable BECAUSE energy is quantized. Old quantum theory reaches its peak.

events.title: Energy levels are real
events.discovery: Electrons colliding with mercury atoms lose energy only in discrete 4.9 eV chunks.
events.evidence: Current through mercury vapor drops sharply at voltage multiples of 4.9 V; the atoms then glow at exactly the matching UV line.
events.significance: Direct, mechanical proof of Bohr's discrete levels - quantization observed in a collision, not just in light.

events.title: Stimulated emission
events.discovery: An excited atom can be triggered by passing light to emit an identical photon (A and B coefficients).
events.evidence: Theoretical derivation that re-obtains Planck's law and assigns momentum h*nu/c to light quanta.
events.significance: The principle inside every laser - written 44 years before the first laser exists. Quantum theory begins predicting technology.

events.title: Space quantization
events.discovery: Silver atoms in a magnetic field split into exactly TWO beams - their magnetic orientation is quantized, not continuous.
events.evidence: Atomic beam through an inhomogeneous magnet left two discrete traces on the plate, not a smear.
events.significance: The measurement that reveals spin before spin is named (1925). Today it's the canonical example of quantum measurement itself.

events.title: Photons carry momentum
events.discovery: X-rays scattering off electrons shift wavelength exactly as if particle-like photons collide billiard-style with electrons.
events.evidence: Measured wavelength shift vs angle matched the photon-collision formula precisely.
events.significance: The last holdouts surrender: light quanta are undeniably real particles with energy AND momentum. Duality is now unavoidable.

events.title: Matter waves
events.discovery: If light waves are particles, then particles are waves: every particle has wavelength lambda = h/p.
events.evidence: PhD thesis; immediately explains Bohr's orbits as standing electron waves. Einstein championed it.
events.significance: The symmetry that completes duality and hands Schrodinger his central idea. Confirmed by electron diffraction in 1927.

events.title: Quantum statistics
events.discovery: Photons (and later atoms) obey new counting rules for identical particles; Einstein extends it to matter and predicts Bose-Einstein condensation.
events.evidence: Bose's derivation of Planck's law from pure statistics, sent from Dhaka to Einstein, who translated and extended it.
events.significance: Identical quantum particles are fundamentally indistinguishable - the root of lasers, superfluids, and the BEC finally created in 1995.

events.title: Exclusion principle and spin
events.discovery: No two electrons share the same quantum state (Pauli, January); the needed fourth quantum number is intrinsic spin (Uhlenbeck-Goudsmit, October).
events.evidence: Explains atomic shell structure, the periodic table's periods, and anomalous Zeeman splitting.
events.significance: WHY chemistry exists: Mendeleev's 1869 pattern finally has a mechanism. Matter is rigid because electrons refuse to overlap.

events.title: Matrix mechanics
events.discovery: The first complete quantum mechanics: observables become matrices that don't commute (pq - qp = ih/2pi).
events.evidence: Heisenberg's Helgoland breakthrough (July 1925), formalized in the Born-Jordan and three-man papers; reproduces atomic spectra.
events.significance: Quantum theory becomes a real, self-consistent mechanics - built only from observable quantities, abandoning orbits entirely.

events.title: The wave equation and the probability rule
events.discovery: A wave equation governs de Broglie's matter waves and reproduces hydrogen exactly; Born then shows |psi|^2 gives the PROBABILITY of finding the particle.
events.evidence: Four 1926 papers solving hydrogen, oscillators, perturbations; proven equivalent to matrix mechanics.
events.significance: The equation at the heart of chemistry, materials, and every circuit simulator - including the statevectors in this project's backend. With Born's rule, God starts playing dice.

events.title: The uncertainty principle
events.discovery: Position and momentum cannot both be sharply defined: delta-x * delta-p >= h-bar/2. Not ignorance - nature's structure.
events.evidence: Derived from the non-commuting formalism; gamma-ray microscope thought experiment.
events.significance: Determinism ends as a fundamental principle. Also the reason quantum states can't be copied or perfectly eavesdropped - the seed of quantum cryptography.

events.title: Electrons diffract
events.discovery: Electron beams produce interference patterns off crystals - matter waves are experimentally real.
events.evidence: Nickel-crystal scattering peaks at exactly de Broglie's predicted angles; Thomson's independent foil experiments.
events.significance: Poetic symmetry: J.J. Thomson proved the electron is a particle; his son proved it's a wave. Both won Nobels. Both were right.

events.title: Fifth Solvay: Bohr vs Einstein
events.discovery: The Copenhagen interpretation (complementarity, probabilistic collapse) is debated at the most famous physics conference ever held.
events.evidence: 17 of the 29 attendees were or became Nobel laureates; Einstein's thought-experiment attacks, Bohr's rebuttals.
events.significance: 'God does not play dice' - 'Einstein, stop telling God what to do.' The interpretation debate that still isn't settled.

events.title: Relativistic quantum mechanics
events.discovery: Merging quantum mechanics with special relativity yields an equation that predicts spin automatically - and demands ANTIMATTER.
events.evidence: The Dirac equation's negative-energy solutions; Carl Anderson finds the positron in cosmic rays in 1932.
events.significance: A particle discovered by pure mathematics before any experiment saw it. The template for theory-led physics ever since.

events.title: The neutron; QM gets rigorous foundations
events.discovery: Chadwick identifies the neutron, completing the atom's parts list; von Neumann publishes the mathematical foundations of QM (Hilbert spaces, measurement theory).
events.evidence: Beryllium radiation knocking protons with the kinematics of a neutral, proton-mass particle; von Neumann's 'Mathematische Grundlagen'.
events.significance: The atom is complete, and quantum mechanics gets the rigorous state-vector formalism this project's simulator literally computes in.

events.title: The EPR paradox and Schrodinger's cat
events.discovery: EPR argue that quantum correlations between distant particles imply the theory is incomplete; Schrodinger responds, coins 'entanglement' (Verschrankung), and poses the cat paradox.
events.evidence: Thought experiments only - Bell (1964) will make them testable, Aspect (1982) will run them.
events.significance: The paper meant to kill quantum mechanics instead names its greatest resource. Entanglement is now the fuel of quantum computing, teleportation, and cryptography.

events.title: The transistor
events.discovery: A solid-state amplifier/switch built from semiconductor physics - band theory and quantum tunneling made practical.
events.evidence: The point-contact transistor at Bell Labs, December 1947.
events.significance: Quantum mechanics becomes the foundation of ALL modern electronics. Every classical computer is already a quantum-physics machine - the irony the quantum computing era will complete.

events.title: The Lamb shift
events.discovery: Two hydrogen levels that Dirac's theory says are identical are minutely split - the vacuum itself perturbs the atom.
events.evidence: Microwave spectroscopy resolving a 1057 MHz splitting.
events.significance: The discrepancy that forces quantum field theory: even 'empty' space seethes with fluctuations. QED is built to explain this number.

events.title: Quantum electrodynamics
events.discovery: A complete quantum field theory of light and matter, with renormalization taming the infinities; Feynman diagrams as its language.
events.evidence: Predicts the electron's magnetic moment to ~12 decimal places - the most precisely verified theory in science.
events.significance: The most accurate theory humanity has ever produced. Feynman's path-integral view will later inspire his 1981 quantum computing proposal.

events.title: Many-worlds interpretation
events.discovery: Take the wave equation with total seriousness: no collapse - every measurement outcome occurs, in branching worlds.
events.evidence: A reinterpretation, not a new prediction; ignored for decades, now a leading interpretation.
events.significance: Deutsch will explicitly credit many-worlds thinking when inventing the universal quantum computer in 1985.

events.title: The laser
events.discovery: Coherent light from stimulated emission - Einstein's 1916 mechanism engineered into a device (maser 1954, ruby laser May 1960).
events.evidence: Maiman's flash-pumped ruby rod at Hughes Labs emitting coherent red pulses.
events.significance: The quantum tool that will later trap ions, cool atoms, and drive the gates of trapped-ion quantum computers.

events.title: Information is physical
events.discovery: Erasing one bit costs a minimum energy (Landauer's principle); Bennett shows computation can be made fully reversible (1973).
events.evidence: Thermodynamic analysis of computation; reversible logic constructions.
events.significance: The conceptual bridge between physics and computation - the prehistory of the quantum computing track. Quantum gates are reversible for exactly this reason.

events.title: Bell's theorem
events.discovery: No local hidden-variable theory can reproduce quantum correlations - EPR's 'incompleteness' is experimentally decidable via an inequality.
events.evidence: A mathematical theorem; CHSH (1969) recasts it for real experiments.
events.significance: Philosophy becomes physics. The universe is provably non-local or non-realistic - and entanglement is certified as genuinely new.

events.title: First Bell test
events.discovery: Entangled photon pairs violate Bell's inequality - quantum mechanics wins its first courtroom test against local realism.
events.evidence: Calcium-cascade photon polarization correlations at Berkeley.
events.significance: Entanglement moves from thought experiment to measured fact. Clauser shares the 2022 Nobel for this.

events.title: THE FORK: quantum models of computation
events.discovery: Benioff constructs a quantum-mechanical Turing machine; Manin independently notes quantum systems' exponential descriptive power.
events.evidence: Benioff's Hamiltonian model of reversible quantum computation (Journal of Statistical Physics).
events.significance: The track splits here. Computation is no longer abstract - it must obey, and can exploit, quantum mechanics.

events.title: 'Nature isn't classical, dammit'
events.discovery: Classical computers need exponential resources to simulate quantum systems - so build computers OUT of quantum mechanics to simulate nature.
events.evidence: MIT keynote 'Simulating Physics with Computers' (May 1981, published 1982).
events.significance: The founding speech of quantum computing, and the direct ancestor of this project's VQE Molecular Forge: simulating molecules is exactly what Feynman asked for.

events.title: Quantum cryptography (BB84)
events.discovery: A key-distribution protocol whose security rests on physics: measuring unknown quantum states disturbs them, exposing any eavesdropper.
events.evidence: Built on Wiesner's unpublishable 1970s 'quantum money'; first working demo 1989 over 32 cm.
events.significance: The first quantum information TECHNOLOGY. Today QKD runs on satellites and metro fiber networks.

events.title: The universal quantum computer
events.discovery: Defines the universal quantum Turing machine and exhibits the first task where quantum beats classical (extended with Jozsa, 1992).
events.evidence: Proc. Royal Society paper formalizing quantum parallelism and universality.
events.significance: Quantum computing becomes a rigorous theory of computation with its own complexity classes - not just a physics dream.

events.title: Quantum teleportation protocol
events.discovery: An unknown quantum state can be transmitted exactly using shared entanglement plus two classical bits - without moving the particle.
events.evidence: Six-author theory paper; experimentally realized with photons in 1997 (Zeilinger's and De Martini's groups).
events.significance: Entanglement is a usable channel. Teleportation is now the routing primitive inside quantum networks and error-corrected architectures.

events.title: Shor's algorithm
events.discovery: A quantum computer can factor integers exponentially faster than any known classical method - breaking RSA cryptography.
events.evidence: Polynomial-time quantum factoring via the quantum Fourier transform.
events.significance: The moment governments and industry started paying. Every 'post-quantum cryptography' migration happening today traces to this paper.

events.title: First real quantum gate
events.discovery: Cirac-Zoller propose a CNOT gate on trapped ions; Monroe and Wineland demonstrate it within months on a single beryllium ion.
events.evidence: NIST trapped-ion experiment (December 1995) implementing controlled logic between motional and spin qubits.
events.significance: Quantum computing leaves the whiteboard. Hardware exists.

events.title: Quantum error correction
events.discovery: Quantum information can be protected without measuring it: Shor's 9-qubit code, Steane's 7-qubit code, then threshold theorems.
events.evidence: Explicit codes encoding one logical qubit in several physical qubits, correcting both bit- and phase-flips.
events.significance: Answers the fatal objection ('decoherence kills everything'). The entire modern race - surface codes, logical qubits - runs on this foundation.

events.title: Grover's search algorithm
events.discovery: Quantum computers search an unstructured list of N items in ~sqrt(N) steps - a provable quadratic speedup for a universal task.
events.evidence: Amplitude-amplification algorithm with proven optimality.
events.significance: With Shor, one of the two canonical algorithms every quantum aspirant learns first - and a staple demo for this project's circuit builder.

events.title: First algorithms run on hardware
events.discovery: 2-qubit NMR machines execute Deutsch-Jozsa and Grover's algorithm; by 2001, a 7-spin IBM molecule runs Shor's algorithm to factor 15.
events.evidence: Nuclear-spin ensembles in molecules manipulated by RF pulses; published factoring of 15 = 3 x 5 (2001).
events.significance: Proof of principle complete: real quantum algorithms on real quantum matter, however small.

events.title: The superconducting qubit
events.discovery: Coherent quantum oscillations in a superconducting circuit - a manufactured, chip-based artificial atom.
events.evidence: Cooper-pair box at NEC showing controllable superpositions of charge states.
events.significance: The lineage that leads directly to transmons - the qubits inside the IBM machines this project submits circuits to.

events.title: The DiVincenzo criteria
events.discovery: Five requirements any physical quantum computer must satisfy (scalable qubits, initialization, long coherence, universal gates, measurement).
events.evidence: Influential position paper synthesizing a decade of proposals.
events.significance: The checklist that turned quantum computing into an engineering discipline with comparable platforms.

events.title: First commercial quantum machine
events.discovery: D-Wave One: a 128-qubit superconducting quantum ANNEALER sold to Lockheed Martin (special-purpose optimization, not universal gates).
events.evidence: Commercial sale and installation; years of debate over quantumness and speedup followed.
events.significance: Quantum computing becomes an industry with customers, marketing, and controversy - forcing rigor about what counts as advantage.

events.title: Quantum computing goes on the cloud
events.discovery: IBM Quantum Experience puts a 5-qubit processor on the public internet - anyone can run circuits on real hardware.
events.evidence: Web-based composer and API; millions of user experiments since; grows into Qiskit.
events.significance: Democratization moment - the exact capability (cloud access to real QPUs) this project's 'quantum core' portal is built on.

events.title: Quantum supremacy claim
events.discovery: 53-qubit Sycamore samples random circuits in ~200 seconds, claimed to take classical supercomputers millennia (later reduced, but the milestone stood).
events.evidence: Nature paper with cross-entropy benchmarking; IBM's rebuttal sharpened the debate.
events.significance: First credible claim of a quantum device beating all classical computers at ANY task - the field's Sputnik moment.

events.title: Nobel Prize for entanglement
events.discovery: The prize honors Bell-test experiments (Aspect's 1982 switched-analyzer tests closing loopholes) and pioneering quantum information science.
events.evidence: Decades of increasingly loophole-free Bell violations, culminating in the 2015 loophole-free tests.
events.significance: Official closure of the Einstein-Bohr debate: local realism is dead, and the 'second quantum revolution' is canon.

events.title: Logical qubits arrive
events.discovery: 48 logical qubits encoded in neutral-atom arrays execute algorithms with error-corrected encoding outperforming physical qubits.
events.evidence: Nature paper (December 2023) on programmable logical processors with transversal gates.
events.significance: Error correction stops being theory. The metric of progress shifts from physical qubit counts to LOGICAL qubits.

events.title: Below the error-correction threshold
events.discovery: The 105-qubit Willow chip demonstrates that enlarging a surface code EXPONENTIALLY suppresses logical errors - errors go down as the system grows.
events.evidence: Distance-3/5/7 surface codes each halving logical error rate (Nature, December 2024).
events.significance: The 1995 threshold theorem validated in silicon-adjacent hardware: scaling now helps rather than hurts. Fault tolerance has a working recipe.

events.title: The fault-tolerance race
events.discovery: Microsoft unveils Majorana 1 claiming topological qubits (contested); IBM publishes its roadmap to the Starling fault-tolerant system (~2029); Amazon debuts its Ocelot error-corrected chip.
events.evidence: Public announcements and papers through 2025; scientific scrutiny of topological claims ongoing.
events.significance: The present frontier of the journey - and where this project's users stand when they finish the odyssey: the machine era has begun, unfinished.
